verdict.rationale: Anthropic's Claude Code docs state that skills follow the Agent Skills open standard, which works across multiple AI tools. Anthropic says it published that standard for cross-platform portability, and the spec defines the same SKILL.md-folder format. A hands-on probe confirmed that third-party tooling installed a spec-conformant skill folder from the official repo with no Anthropic account. Community lock-in worries are general skepticism, not concrete counter-evidence. Missing for 10: hands-on proof that the same skill folder runs unchanged in a non-Anthropic agent (the probe targeted claude-code), and guidance on which Claude-specific frontmatter extensions stay portable.

support.subject: As a developer, skills follow the open Agent Skills specification so the same skill folder is valid beyond this one vendor's tooling

citations.quote: Claude Code skills follow the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) open standard, which works across multiple AI tools.
We've published Agent Skills as an open standard for cross-platform portability.
A skill is a directory containing, at minimum, a `SKILL.md` file
the repo's skills are plain, spec-conformant markdown folders installable by third-party tooling, no Anthropic account needed.
